title: Fabrication
description: Recognise fabricated content — citations, quotes, numbers, function names — for what it mechanically is: a plausible shape filled in with made-up specifics, not a lie and not a lookup failure. Learn which kinds of questions produce it most, and how to reduce it without expecting it to hit zero.

title: Verifying Efficiently
description: Check AI output at a cost proportional to what being wrong would actually cost — spot-checks that genuinely find errors instead of just reassuring you, checks against a real source instead of your own memory, and a repeatable routine for work you do over and over.

title: Bias in Practice
description: Detect biased AI output in real tasks by testing it directly — holding a task constant and changing exactly one detail — rather than debating bias in the abstract. Covers where it shows up in ordinary work, how to run a controlled test, the silent defaults that assume a particular kind of person, the specific assumptions models carry about health and disability, and what prompting can and can't fix.

title: Agreement and Flattery
description: Notice when a model is agreeing with the premise you handed it rather than actually answering — where the pull toward agreement comes from mechanically, how a leading question manufactures the answer you went in wanting, how to ask in a way that genuinely permits disagreement, how to use a model to argue against your own position for real, and when the right move is not asking a model at all.

title: What It Cannot Do
description: State a model's current limits precisely enough to stop wasting effort on them — the specific things it's oddly bad at (letter counts, large arithmetic), what it structurally cannot know past a training cutoff, tasks where 'usually right' is worthless regardless of the hit rate, judgment calls that aren't yours to delegate, and a habit for keeping your own picture of its limits from going stale as models change.
